title: Compatibility: Meshes disappear in a viewport with positional_shadow_atlas_size = 0 when another viewport shadows the same light
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: v4.6.2.stable.official [71f334935] (macOS editor run and official web export templates) and v4.8.dev, master [18a63d15e], built locally. - Fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123051 - Not tested earlier than 4.6.2; the code shape is present at least back through 4.6. ### System information macOS 26 - Godot v4.6.2.stable - Compatibility (gl_compatibility / WebGL 2) - Apple M2 Max ### Issue description **Context:** I hit this while building live CCTV monitors for a game. A SubViewport renders a yard through cameras, and I set shadow atlas to 0 for performance in web. ### What happens Two viewports render in the same frame and share a world: 1. The main viewport has the default shadow atlas and an `OmniLight3D` with `shadow_enabled = true`, drawing shadows. 2. A `SubViewport` has `positional_shadow_atlas_size = 0` — the class reference recommends this to save performance: *"If this is set to 0, no positional shadows will be visible at all."* **Expected:** the SubViewport shows the same scene, lit, just without positional shadows. **Actual:** every mesh that light touches is missing from the SubViewport. In the MRP that is all five meshes, so the SubViewport is completely empty. No errors, no warnings. Any non-zero atlas size brings the picture back. *(The MRP gives the sub-camera a red background, so an empty feed shows up as a labeled red rectangle.)* This is not a web bug. It breaks the same way on desktop macOS, and 4.6.2-stable and master render the broken frame byte-for-byte the same. On the web it reproduces in Chrome under ANGLE-Metal, `--use-angle=gl`, and `--use-angle=swiftshader`. ### Why it happens Both steps are in `drivers/gles3/rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp`: 1. **The light is misclassified.** `_fill_render_list()` (master ~1367/1390) calls a light "shadowed" from `light_has_shadow()` and the cached `shadow_id`. Both are global light state, written when *any* viewport grants the light an atlas slot. The atlas-less viewport inherits that verdict and files the light into `light_passes`. 2. **The base pass is skipped.** Pass 0 of the color loop (master ~3404) then checks whether the light has a slot in *this* render's atlas: ```cpp if (pass < int32_t(inst->light_passes.size())) { RID light_instance_rid = inst->light_passes[pass].light_instance_rid; if (!GLES3::LightStorage::get_singleton()->light_instance_has_shadow_atlas(light_instance_rid, p_render_data->shadow_atlas)) { // Shadow wasn't able to get a spot on the atlas. So skip it. continue; } } ``` On a zero-size atlas it never does. `shadow_atlas_update_light()` returns false at its `size == 0` early-out, so the `continue` runs. The comment means "skip this shadow", but on pass 0 it skips the mesh's base draw. The mesh never renders. This is also why the workaround works: a real atlas lets the viewport grant the light its own slot, so the check passes. The allocation alone is the fix; no shadow ever renders into it. ### How it was confirmed - A WebGL interception harness on the exported build (wrapping `useProgram`, the draw calls, framebuffer and viewport state) shows the SubViewport drawing each mesh once, with the depth-only program, at `atlas = 0`. The color-pass draws are simply absent. From `atlas = 256` up it issues the same depth + color draws as the main viewport. - In the game, this appeared on the web as flat white silhouettes and a console flood of `INVALID_OPERATION: uniformMatrix4fv/uniform3fv: location is not from the associated program`. ### Workaround Set any non-zero `positional_shadow_atlas_size` (256 is enough) on the affected viewport. The only cost is the atlas allocation. ### Steps to reproduce **With the attached MRP:** 1. Run the project with `--atlas=0`, e.g. `godot --path atlas_zero_test -- --atlas=0`. The white-framed rectangle is the SubViewport. It stays an empty red box: that is the bug. 2. Run it again with `--atlas=512`. The rectangle now shows the scene. Two more flags for narrowing it down: `--noshadow` turns off the lamp's shadows (the picture returns even at atlas 0, so the shadow grant is the trigger), and `--dirshadow` adds a shadowed DirectionalLight3D (nothing changes; directional shadows do not use the positional atlas). **From scratch:** 1. Make a scene with a few textured meshes, a `Camera3D`, and an `OmniLight3D` with `shadow_enabled = true` close enough to light them. 2. Add a `SubViewport` sharing the same world. Give it its own `Camera3D` aimed at the same meshes, set `positional_shadow_atlas_size = 0` and `render_target_update_mode = UPDATE_ALWAYS`, and show its texture on a `TextureRect`. 3. Run with the Compatibility renderer. Every mesh the light touches is missing from the SubViewport. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [mrp-zero-atlas-subviewport.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31657745/mrp-zero-atlas-subviewport.zip) Three files, 2.6 KB, no `.godot` folder. Run with the Compatibility renderer; `--atlas=0` shows the bug, `--atlas=512` the workaround.
